seed: GI numbers for the lasso cyclase, lasso protease (leader peptidase) and RRE of all known lasso peptides (28 characterized BGCs)
tool: BLAST-P against the nr database in GenBank "returning the top 1,000 hits for each with default settings"; then RODEO, which "combines hidden Markov model-based analysis, heuristic scoring, and machine learning", retrieving sequences from GenBank and comparing against Pfam with HMMER3
iterations: Hits were ranked by maximum similarity to any query sequence, and the top local genomic region (6 genes in either direction of cyclase) of top hits were sequentially analyzed with RODEO until no new lasso peptide-like BGCs were returned; the search was then re-seeded: "we repeated the above using as queries representative lasso peptide cyclases, obtained during the first search, from the Bacteroidetes, Cyanobacteria, Firmicutes, Fusobacteria, and Veruccomicrobia, and Archaea"
target_db: GenBank nr; Pfam database
search_unit: protein, then the surrounding genomic region
curation: BGC definition: "Lasso peptide BGCs were defined by the local presence of genes encoding proteins matching the Pfams for the lasso cyclase, leader peptidase, and RRE"; clusters with only one identifiable E, B or C protein and no precursor discarded; borderline clusters retained only if they "contained two or more identifiable lasso biosynthetic genes and showed high similarity to valid BGCs, as judged by network connectivity"
context_step: 6 genes in either direction of cyclase; RODEO predicts the function of genes flanking a query protein, output as spreadsheet and HTML
clustering: SSN of the lasso cyclases used as the arbiter for ambiguous clusters
downstream: precursor prediction (see Q-NT row), SSNs, trees, MALDI-TOF-MS screening, NMR structures
scale: 4,672 potential BGCs with 25,506 potential precursor peptides from the merged searches, refined to 1,419 lasso peptide BGCs; antiSMASH identified 87% of the same BGCs; the antiSMASH Database predicted only 351
published_artifacts: Supplementary Data Sets 1-3 (RODEO spreadsheets, SSN files, Circos inputs), Supplementary Tables 1-3 (heuristic features, SVM features, tool comparison) and the source code at ripprodeo.org; no files under lit/supp for this stem

seed: the intergenic regions inside each of the 1,419 candidate BGCs
tool: RODEO "performed a six-frame translation of the intergenic regions within each of the potential 1,419 BGCs"; heuristic linear-combination scoring S = A.X; MEME (parameters: -nmotif 16 -mod zoops) for the top 16 motifs and FIMO to scan all peptides; SVM via libsvm with "an rbf kernel with C = 25, gamma = 2.75E-06, and auto class weight"
iterations: one translation pass; iterative weight optimisation of the heuristic score and SVM grid search
target_db: the BGC intergenic regions themselves (not a public database)
search_unit: six-frame nucleotide translation of intergenic regions
curation: peptides "assessed based on length and essential sequence features and split into predicted leader and core regions"; motif score from FIMO counted only if >1; manual curation of a ~25% training sample into lasso/non-lasso/indeterminate; 80/20 training/validation split "to avoid over-fitting"; disagreements between SVM class and linear score inspected by hand; abnormal SSN clustering inspected; "although correct in 94% of cases, 75 required manual adjustment" of the leader/core split
context_step: the BGC itself is the context; precursor location relative to the C, E and B genes recorded
clustering: SSN of precursors at alignment score cutoff 1E-6 used to sanity-check SVM calls
downstream: SSNs, trees, residue composition analysis, GREMLIN coevolution, MS and NMR characterisation of five new lasso peptides
scale: 1,315 lasso precursor peptides from >24,000 candidate peptides (25,506 candidates); SVM precision 97.9% and recall 92.8%, estimated to give ~30 false positives and ~100 false negatives over the whole set; ~85% of final precursors were not annotated as coding sequences in GenBank
published_artifacts: Supplementary Data (MEME motif files used by FIMO), Supplementary Tables 1-2 (features), Python scripts at ripprodeo.org

seed: the 1,315 predicted precursors and the biosynthetic proteins (RREs, leader proteases, lasso cyclases)

target_db: the RODEO-derived sequence sets

published_artifacts: Supplementary Data Set 2 (SSN files)

seed: the 1,419 BGCs and their precursor/RRE pairs
tool: paired alignment of precursor peptides and RREs (PF05402 in lasso BGCs), RRE sequences aligned "using MUSCLE on default settings in MEGA7", precursor and RRE alignments concatenated; GREMLIN web server (http://gremlin.bakerlab.org/) "on default settings, filtered at 75% gap removal and 25% coverage thresholds. No multiple sequence alignment (MSA) generation was performed"; MEME 4.11.1 "(parameters: -nmotif 8 -mod zoops)" and FIMO; HHpred modeling toolkit for the RRE homology model (template LynD, PDB 4V1T, aligned residues 8-84)

seed: subsets of non-coding intergenic regions (IGRs); no sequence or model seed - the structure is discovered de novo in each IGR cluster
tool: BLAST-based subsequence clustering with a reimplementation of the earlier algorithm ("weinberg-overcluster2", single-linkage clustering on subsequences of IGRs, so that "subsequences in a given IGR can participate in separate clusters"), then "an updated CMfinder, version 0.4.1, that extends the previous software version primarily to handle fragmentary sequence contigs in which RNA sequences are sometimes truncated"; RNIE for Rho-independent terminators; R2R for drawings
iterations: manual iterative refinement per candidate: "we analyzed the most promising candidates in a process that centered on additional homology searches and attempts to improve structural predictions with help from CMfinder"; no automatic convergence criterion
target_db: In total, we analyzed 237 Gb (237 x 109 bp) of sequences, with 54 Gb genomic and 183 Gb metagenomic sequences. These sequences contained 37 Gb of IGRs; sources chiefly RefSeq, IMG/M, MG-RAST and GenBank; genes annotated with the Conserved Domain Database version 2.25 and RNAs with Rfam version 12.1
curation: scoring by "a combination of an updated RNAphylo, and a new method called hmmpair", each converted to a percentile within ~250,000 reference alignments with the final score the minimum of the two percentiles; manual evaluation of covariation with explicit warning that "non-biological covariation can result, for example, from aligning sequences that are not homologous, or by aligning non-homologous regions of homologous sequences"; "most candidate ncRNAs initially predicted lacked convincing covariation and were not further pursued"; RNAcode run to exclude protein-coding regions (best P ~0.001, E ~0.22 over 224 motifs); motifs with significant Rfam matches not reported
context_step: genetic context is the functional evidence: potential 5-prime UTR assignment, downstream and upstream gene domains, terminator and Shine-Dalgarno presence; for three motifs the associated protein was confirmed by searching a nearby protein with "the hmmsearch and jackhmmer programs from HMMER 3.1b2 (default parameters, except we used an E-value threshold of 10-3 with hmmsearch)" and counting homologs "encoded within 6 Kbases"
clustering: single-linkage clustering of IGR subsequences by BLAST score; each motif is a covariance model
downstream: in-line probing and ribozyme/riboswitch assays on selected motifs; Rfam and term-seq comparisons
scale: 224 novel ncRNA classes; ROOL RNAs average 581 nt; 13 motifs meet all three criteria for sophisticated function; ~250,000 alignments used for score normalisation; no CPU time reported
published_artifacts: lit/supp/2017_Weinberg_Lünse_Corbino_Breaker_224_Candidate_Structured_RNAs/gkx699_supp.zip contains 224 Stockholm alignments without annotation (nar-01080-r-2017-File009.zip, sto-just-motif/*.sto, each with a #=GF ORIGINAL_MOTIF provenance line naming the database, lineage and CMfinder parameters), 224 fully annotated alignments (File010.zip, sto-with-annot/), 52 bSCRAP alignments (File013.zip), the two libsvm riboswitch models up0.model/up1.model with their .range scaling files (File014.zip), SupplFile-6-Excel-updated.xlsx (Tables S1-S10: per-motif taxa, counts, average length and the analysis method that found it; 1,159 metagenomic data sources; 14,589 species; ribozyme and riboswitch assay constructs) and the 224-motif supplementary PDF

seed: IGRs grouped by the conserved domain of their immediately downstream gene (and, in a variant, by proximity to chosen gene classes)
tool: IGR selection code plus the same overcluster2/CMfinder pipeline; "we cluster all IGRs by domains in their immediately downstream gene and then further cluster each domain-specific set of IGRs as usual using BLAST and overcluster2"; conserved domains taken from the Conserved Domain Database, "all available domains are used"

target_db: all IGRs in the 237 Gb corpus; CDD version 2.25
search_unit: IGR, selected by the domain of the flanking gene

scale: Supplementary Table S6: "Lineage and environment" 153 subsets, "Large IGRs" 1, "Cluster by downstream gene" 47,831, "Nearby to genetic elements" 7

seed: IGRs selected by size, by terminator presence, or by cross-database comparison
tool: large-IGR strategy: "only IGRs of at least 600 bp were considered"; terminator strategy: RNIE terminator predictions plus G+C content of "the 100 nucleotides upstream of each predicted terminator", classified with Support Vector Machines "as implemented by Libsvm version 3.17" using four features, svm-scale -l -1 -u 1, grid.py parameter search, svm-train -b 1, and "Lines in up0.predictions with SVM probabilities greater than or equal to 0.9 are predicted as containing a" riboswitch; RefSeq-versus-metagenome strategy: MetaPhlAn used to pick metagenomes "in which at least 0.01% of contigs were predicted as coming from this phylum"
target_db: the same 237 Gb corpus; RefSeq version 63 for the lineage side of the cross-database strategy
curation: contig-edge control stated twice: "IGRs within 800 bp of the end of a contig could be misannotated if a truncated gene was not detected, and so these IGRs were also discarded", and in the SVM filter "Either side of the IGR is within 800 nucleotides of the end of the containing contig. In such cases, the annotation of the IGR is considered uncertain"; IGRs with any degenerate nucleotide (N) discarded; IGRs whose downstream gene is oriented towards the IGR discarded; IGRs containing a predicted T-box RNA (RF00230) discarded; negative training examples drawn from IGRs not predicted to contain riboswitches, with homologous IGRs noted as a residual leakage risk

downstream: the SVM-selected IGR sets fed into the same motif-discovery pipeline
scale: large-IGR input set "totaled 1.4 billion bp, which proved manageable"; the full 37 Gb IGR set was judged infeasible because "the computational time and memory required for analysis expands with many IGRs" and because "the false positive rate when IGRs are compared increases with their total number"; the cross-database strategy omits metagenome-versus-metagenome comparisons to cut the false positive rate; SVM sensitivity 24-56% and positive predictive value 6-38% per lineage (Suppl. Tab. S10)
published_artifacts: libsvm model files up0.model, up0.range, up1.model, up1.range in lit/supp/2017_Weinberg_Lünse_Corbino_Breaker_224_Candidate_Structured_RNAs/gkx699_supp.zip!nar-01080-r-2017-File014.zip; Suppl. Tab. S9 and S10 give the riboswitch training/test split and per-lineage performance

seed: the 224 finished motif alignments, used as covariance models for cross-checking

downstream: Suppl. Tab. S5 overlap table; term-seq concordance analysis
scale: only 1 of 224 motifs overlapped a term-seq prediction; only 3 of 224 are present in the three term-seq genomes; Rfam overlaps rare (Suppl. Tab. S5 lists 17)
published_artifacts: Suppl. Tab. S2 and S5 in SupplFile-6-Excel-updated.xlsx; all 224 alignments in File009/File010 zips

seed: individual candidate ESP sequences
tool: PFAM, SMART and "Hmmpred" (HHpred) "for remote homology detection, the protein structure prediction tool Phyre2 for homology modelling"; models "viewed and analysed further using Chimera"

seed: the per-cluster counts of occurrences inside bait neighborhoods and in the whole database
tool: three relevance metrics computed by CalculateICITY.sh / GetIcityForBLASTHits.py: (1) "icity" = w'/w where w is the effective size of all members of the permissive cluster and w' the effective size of members in the vicinity of the seeds; (2) median distance to the bait, computed over strict-cluster representatives; (3) effective abundance in the whole database. Effective size = number of strict clusters at MMseqs2 sequence identity 0.9 (default coverage), which is the explicit correction for sequencing/clonal bias (counts otherwise biased ">10,000:1" between e.g. E. coli and Buttiauxella gaviniae)

curation: candidate selection either by thresholds ("icity" > 0.6 and distance < 5 in the CRISPR-Cas study; cutoffs from earlier work: "icity" > 0.7, effective distance < 2 (distance < 5 is optimal as well), effective abundance >= 1) or by voxel classification of the 3-D metric space; "Clusters with an effective abundance in the genomic database equal to 1 should be discarded or manually reviewed"
context_step: distance-to-bait is itself one of the metrics
clustering: strict MMseqs2 clustering at 0.9 as the normalization device
downstream: F0.5 optimization: metrics space split by icity 0.1, log abundance 0.5, distance 1; best sector gives F0.5 = 0.98, precision 0.98 (48 known non-Cas families among 2,624 in the sector), recall 0.96 (2,576 of 2,678 known Cas families)
scale: ~30 min for the example dataset; benchmark numbers from the 50,000-genome CRISPRicity analysis
